E1.source: D06 Documentation-Time Baseline · Epic Signal 18-month trace
E1.reference: 18 months of Epic Signal documentation-time data across Meridian's 14 hospitals and 220 ambulatory sites · median clinician logs 1 hr 48 min/day of after-hours Epic activity (pajama time) · 47% of Meridian physicians above specialty-benchmark median · primary-care and hospital-medicine cohorts most exposed.

E2.source: D06 Documentation-Time Baseline · MBI-HSS burnout survey wave
E2.reference: MBI-HSS burnout survey wave completed 2026-01-12 · n=1,240 attending physicians and APPs · emotional exhaustion subscale shows 54% of clinicians in the elevated band · correlation with documentation time r=0.41 (p<0.01) · Depersonalisation subscale 38% elevated.

E3.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Sarah Chen (CIO) transcript
E3.reference: CIO framing: 'Abridge / DAX Copilot / Suki were deployed to solve three different clinician populations · what we don't have is a value chain · the question is not which vendor survives, it's how any of them connect to CDI, HCC capture, and quality measure capture.'

E4.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Dr. Larsson (CMO) transcript
E4.reference: CMO framing: 'Our north-star is clinician cognitive load · if we only chase HCC capture uplift we are just moving documentation burden to a different accountant · pajama time is the number I can take to my medical staff and they believe it.'

E5.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Priya Raman (VP Revenue Cycle) transcript
E5.reference: Revenue Cycle framing: on the MA book the HCC recapture gap is real and material · estimate $3.2-5.1M/yr of uncaptured risk-adjustment across the MA-heavy payer mix · DRG specificity on inpatient side shows similar downgrade pattern worth $1.8-2.6M/yr in CMI drift.

E6.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Dr. Morales (CMIO) transcript
E6.reference: CMIO framing: three parallel ambient vendors is an unstable equilibrium · Abridge handles primary care well, DAX Copilot carries specialty workflows, Suki covers outpatient procedural · but governance is fragmented across three vendor councils and note-template drift is measurable · argued for earlier consolidation; deferred to Phase 3 decision memo.

E7.source: Ambient Clinical Value Chain pattern · pattern manifest record
E7.reference: AbarVa Transformation Genome pattern `ambient-clinical-value-chain` · frames ambient listening as the platform for a clinical value chain (documentation → CDI → HCC capture → quality measure capture → care-gap closure) rather than a scribe product · 10 triggering symptoms · 8 detection signals · recommended intervention set anchored on value-chain integration rather than vendor consolidation.

E8.source: D03 Success Metric Tree · north-star metric framing
E8.reference: Primary metric: clinician after-hours Epic time (pajama time) in minutes/clinician/day · supporting metrics: note turnaround time (sign-to-close), HCC capture rate on MA panel, CDI query resolution cycle time, quality-measure documentation capture rate · MBI-HSS burnout index held as quarterly trailing indicator.

E9.source: D16 Business Case · value-at-stake model · Phase 3 baseline lock
E9.reference: Steady-state value-at-stake: $8-14M/yr · cognitive-load recovery component $3-5M/yr (retention and recruitment arbitrage, locum avoidance, visit-volume recovery) · documentation quality component $5-9M/yr (HCC recapture $3.2-5.1M/yr · DRG specificity $1.8-2.6M/yr · quality-measure performance $0.5-1.3M/yr) · capital envelope $4.2M · 12-18 month payback.

E10.source: D10 Benchmark Comparison · cohort analysis · ambient maturity
E10.reference: 6-IDN composite cohort · Meridian is the only cohort member operating three ambient vendors in parallel past 12 months · 4 of 6 peers consolidated to a single primary within 18 months of first deployment · 2 peers operate a primary + specialty pairing · cohort median HCC recapture lift post-ambient: 4-7 points on MA book when integrated to CDI; <1 point when not.

E11.source: D08 Pain Point Register · documentation governance audit
E11.reference: Note-template drift audit: sampled 2,400 ambient-generated notes across the three vendors over 90 days · 23% show specialty-inappropriate template selection · 11% show HCC-relevant language present in transcript but absent from final note · primary driver: no shared CDI feedback loop between vendors.

E12.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Abridge vendor council representative
E12.reference: Abridge vendor council: 'We treat Meridian as a flagship primary-care ambient deployment · we have HCC-oriented code suggestion available but it has not been enabled at Meridian because integration to Epic HCC queue has not been commissioned on the Meridian side.'

E13.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · DAX Copilot vendor council representative
E13.reference: DAX Copilot (Microsoft) vendor council: 'Specialty deployments at Meridian cover cardiology, orthopedics, and GI · clinician adoption steady but DRG specificity feedback loop has not been opened · we have the capability but it requires CDI integration on Meridian's side.'

E14.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · Suki vendor council representative
E14.reference: Suki vendor council: 'Outpatient procedural deployment · Meridian uses Suki primarily in urgent care and outpatient surgery · lighter integration footprint · no current HCC or DRG feedback loop commissioned.'

E15.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · CDI director shadow
E15.reference: CDI director framing: 'We run 42 CDI specialists across the system · since ambient deployed we have received almost no change in query volume routed from ambient notes · the ambient vendors are not routing documentation gaps to our queue · this is the biggest missed integration in the program.'

E16.reference: Sponsor working session · Sarah Chen · Dr. Larsson · Priya Raman · Dr. Morales · agreed to charter the program around value-chain activation rather than vendor rationalization · agreed to preserve the three-vendor envelope through Phase 3 decision memo · agreed pajama time is the north-star metric.

E17.reference: Specialty decomposition of pajama time: primary care 2 hr 09 min/day median · hospital medicine 1 hr 54 min/day · cardiology 1 hr 32 min/day · orthopedics 1 hr 17 min/day · urgent care 48 min/day · ambulatory surgery 42 min/day · ambient vendor coverage unevenly distributed across these specialties.

E18.source: D01 Charter · payer mix and risk contract exposure
E18.reference: Meridian payer mix: Medicare Advantage + commercial risk-based 55% of revenue · traditional Medicare 22% · Medicaid 14% · commercial fee-for-service 9% · substantial ACO / MSSP exposure · HCC capture is a direct revenue mechanism on MA book, not an accounting artifact.

E19.source: D04 Intake Synthesis · chief ambulatory officer field shadow
E19.reference: Chief Ambulatory Officer framing: 'The 220 ambulatory sites are where the clinician burnout math actually lives · if we get ambient working in ambulatory primary care, we buy capacity worth 6-9 incremental visits per clinician per week · that is a real patient-access number.'

E20.source: D06 Workstream Charters · Phase 2 steering ratification · 2026-02-03
E20.reference: Phase 2 four-workstream charter approved by steering committee · WS1 documentation governance (Dr. Morales + Theo J.), WS2 clinician burnout measurement (Dr. Larsson + Kevin B.), WS3 vendor rationalisation candidates (Priya Raman + Dr. Morales), WS4 CMIO/CMO alignment cadence (Sarah Chen + Dr. Larsson) · workstream-level Tier-2 authority bounds and cross-workstream coordination via Nexus orchestrator surface.

E21.source: D08 Pain Point Register · Phase 2 intake corpus
E21.reference: Phase 2 pain-point intake corpus: 22 structured clinician conversations (12 primary care, 6 specialty, 4 outpatient procedural), 4 CDI-specialist shadows, 6 revenue-cycle workshops, 3 vendor-council joint reviews · conducted 2026-02-05 → 2026-02-24 · 28 distinct pain points logged.

E22.source: D08 Pain Point Register · three-axis severity scoring
E22.reference: Three-axis scoring matrix: severity (clinician-impact + dollar-impact composite), feasibility (12-month recoverability inside $4.2M envelope), program-relevance (ambient-value-chain vs. adjacent-program) · 10 high-severity pains / 13 medium / 5 low · top 4 by weighted program-relevance: primary-care pajama time, note-template drift, CDI-queue starvation, reporting latency.

E23.source: D08 Pain Point Register · clinician-voice triangulation
E23.reference: 22 clinician conversations decomposed by finding: pajama-time variance across 220 ambulatory sites ranges 1.42-2.38 hr/day median · in-basket and message volume consumes 38 min/day median in primary care · visit-volume compensation pressure surfaced in 14 of 22 conversations · 9 of 14 primary-care clinicians flagged post-visit care-gap documentation load as an ambient non-coverage pain.

E24.source: D08 Pain Point Register · Epic template proliferation audit
E24.reference: Epic template proliferation in primary care: 17 active templates across the 3 largest primary-care specialties · vendor-specific template governance cadences: Abridge weekly, DAX Copilot monthly, Suki quarterly · 40 clinicians across specialty and hospital medicine work in dual-ambient settings (two vendors active).

E25.source: D08 / D10 · CDI-queue routing volume benchmark
E25.reference: Pattern-evidence CDI-queue benchmark for Meridian's scale and MA-payer-mix: expected 180-220 HCC-relevant queries/week and 120-160 DRG-specificity queries/week · observed at Meridian: ~40 HCC queries/week, ~35 DRG queries/week · delta is the empirical measure of the ambient-to-CDI integration gap.

E26.source: D08 Pain Point Register · data/IT cluster reporting latency
E26.reference: Reporting latency state: CDI-queue, HCC-capture, pajama-time dashboards close on T+21 cycle · vendor telemetry fragmented across three ambient vendors with no unified Meridian-side surface · Epic integration middleware runs three separate connectors commissioned by different project teams without automated integration-surface tests · patient-facing watchlist (consent fatigue, portal-summary accuracy concerns, ambient-active preference variance) routed to D22 change-management package.

E27.source: D10 Benchmark Comparison · 5-peer IDN cohort selection
E27.reference: Cohort selection · four-filter methodology: revenue band $5.5B-$11B · hospital count 8-19 · ambulatory footprint 150-260 sites · payer mix ≥45% MA and commercial risk-based · auxiliary tests: ambient vendor live ≥18 months, CDI team 25-65 specialists · final cohort size 5 · no individual peer identifiable · ratified by Priya Raman 2026-02-18, re-validated by Dr. Morales 2026-02-26.

E28.source: D10 Benchmark Comparison · cohort scorecard · ambient value-chain integration maturity
E28.reference: Meridian cohort position: 4th quartile on ambient-value-chain integration maturity · 3rd quartile on pajama time · 2nd quartile on ambient-vendor clinician adoption · HCC capture 58% (cohort median 62%, top-quartile 71%) · pajama-time primary care 2 hr 09 min/day vs. cohort median 1 hr 51 min · note sign-to-close 3.8 hr vs. cohort median 3.6 hr · four transferable practices: unified telemetry, HCC feedback loop, quality-measure capture, template governance.

E29.reference: MBI-HSS cohort comparison · 4 of 5 cohort peers publish/share anonymised MBI-HSS wave data (fifth runs a different instrument) · Meridian emotional-exhaustion 54% vs. 4-peer cohort median 48% (range 42-56%) · depersonalisation Meridian 38% vs. cohort median 35% · two peers reduced emotional-exhaustion 8-11 points after integrating ambient into CDI and HCC workflows.

E30.source: D10 Benchmark Comparison · Peer-3 deep dive · payer-provider hybrid
E30.reference: Peer-3 deep dive: payer-provider hybrid IDN · ~60% MA exposure · ~$6.8B revenue · single ambient vendor consolidated 19 months post-deployment · pajama time 14% below cohort median · HCC capture 9 points above cohort median · CDI routing 2.4× cohort median · pattern-library decomposition: ~70% of Peer-3 lift integration-driven (portable), ~30% consolidation-driven + captive-MA-specific (partially non-portable to Meridian).

E31.source: D11 Hypothesis Backlog · hypothesis resolution workshop 2026-03-03
E31.reference: Hypothesis resolution workshop · Sarah Chen, Dr. Larsson, Priya Raman, Dr. Morales · 12 hypotheses tested: 7 validated, 2 rejected, 2 deferred to Phase 5, 1 held open for D17 · four-cluster structure (consolidation, documentation redesign, clinician-facing workflow, governance) · parallel-track sequencing over sequential selected · H12 rationalisation hypothesis explicitly routed to D17 under charter commitment.

E32.reference: AbarVa pattern-library lever-interaction model for ambient-clinical-value-chain: parallel-track execution of CDI integration, HCC feedback loop, and template governance produces +25-35% faster outcome realisation vs. sequential execution · compounding mechanism: CDI-queue volume reinforces HCC feedback loop reinforces template governance on a positive cycle · additive-only low-scenario assumes zero compounding for conservative business-case framing.
